title: Splitness and the new nondegenerate set from top degeneracies
statement: Let K be split and suppose L restricts strictly to K, with its top family identified with attachedFamily K V [def-weil-pbc-site-split-attachment-data]. Assume every epi from top degree to an old degree acts on indices by concatenating with the unique normalized old label, and all its component maps are isomorphisms. Then L is split, and an index of its top family is nondegenerate exactly when it is the image of a new V-index under the top-family identification.

proof.text: Substitute the restriction equality. In an old degree, any degeneracy factor lands in a still smaller old degree, so nondegeneracy is equivalent in L and its restriction. Embed restricted labels into L and invert the embedding using the dimension inequality for epis. This equivalence identifies the old label-index maps and their components, transferring bijectivity and component isomorphisms from K.

A nondegenerate old index normalizes to its identity label: this identity label maps to the index by K.map_id, and normalization is inverse to the bijective label map. Consequently every old top label is in the image of its own proper epi, whereas no new index is in any proper epi image. Use injectivity of the top equality transport and disjointness of sum constructors. This proves exactly the claimed nondegenerate set.

A top label either has old target, where it is a retained label, or top target, where its epi is the identity and its index is a new nondegenerate one. This exhaustive classification and the two disjoint sum summands prove injectivity and surjectivity of the top label-index map. Old-target components are isomorphisms by the assumed epi API; identity-label components are identities by L.map_id. Combine this with old splitness.
